concept.name: Residual
concept.definition: The difference between an observed response and the value fitted by a model, e_i = y_i - f(x_i; beta_hat). Residuals are the observable proxies for the unobservable error terms and the primary diagnostic for model adequacy.
concept.intuition: The leftover after the model has said its piece: if the model captured the structure, the leftovers should look like pure noise with nothing left to exploit.
concept.mechanics: Residuals are computed from the fitted model and examined graphically (against fitted values, regressors, and time order) for nonlinearity, non-constant variance, drift, autocorrelation, and non-normality; formal tests such as Breusch-Pagan or Ljung-Box complement the plots. Standardized and studentized versions flag outliers.
concept.formula: e_i = y_i - f(x_i; beta_hat); in OLS with an intercept the residuals satisfy sum e_i = 0 and X'e = 0.
concept.failure_modes: Structured residuals signal misspecification, but pattern-free residuals do not prove the model is right: they cannot reveal omitted variables uncorrelated with the included ones. In time series, ignored residual autocorrelation invalidates standard errors.
concept.misconceptions: That residuals are the same as the true errors: residuals are estimates constrained by the fit (they sum to zero and are mutually correlated), so their distribution only approximates that of the errors.
concept.example: After fitting an AR(1) to returns, the Ljung-Box test on squared residuals still shows correlation, meaning the variance structure remains unmodeled and motivating a GARCH extension.

citations.source: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 4.4.4 How can I tell if a model fits my data?
